evidence: bp-service.lisp:1054-1055 `(loop until (eq (fnn-core 'fn-bpfj-finishedp job) t) do (setq job (fnn-core 'fn-bpfj-step job +fnn-bps-fragment-quantum+)))`. The outer `(loop ...)` at 1040 repeats this for each candidate family. It is reached from fnn-bps-receive line 1117-1118 `(when (eq (first result) :accepted) (fnn-bps-fragment-progress service))`, which runs inside *fnn-tcl-deliver* while the final XFER_ACK is held. The constant's docstring claims "the work of one scheduling step, whatever the family holds".
fix: Make the reassembly job resumable across scheduling steps: keep it in the service, step one quantum per wakeup or tick, and run it after the ACK is flushed rather than inside the delivery callback.
notes: 2026-10-03 source consumer now retains arrival/job/limit/family-key, one sweep quantum per service turn, after custody ACK; idle listener and diagnostic once preserve continuation. Actual shipped raw caller/EOF/keepalive/once tests pass; full image/proof/cost/funding still open.
reviewer: bp-service.lisp:1054-1055 loops fn-bpfj-step until fn-bpfj-finishedp with no yield, and the outer loop (1040) can do this for more families. fnn-bps-receive (1117-1118) calls fnn-bps-fragment-progress, which also drives the publication effects, from inside the deliver callback. fnn-tcl-act holds the final ACK in the held list until settlement and flush (tcpcl.lisp:391-404, 449). The whole reassembly and its publication therefore run before the ACK goes out, with no keepalive or session tick. The quantum bounds one ACL2 call, not one scheduling step, contrary to its docstring (1019-1022) and the D27 rule that exhausting a quantum should yield. The work is bounded by the profile's held octets, so the impact is latency/timeout risk, not unbounded work.
scenario: A peer sends the last fragment of a large family (up to the profile's held octets). The host performs the whole reassembly sweep (and any further ready families) synchronously, sending no keepalives and releasing no ACK. The peer's idle or transfer timer can expire after kind-5 custody is durable, so it retransmits. The single-threaded node is meanwhile unresponsive. The 4096-position quantum bounds nothing at the scheduling level (D27: exhausting a quantum should yield).
title: Fragment reassembly runs to completion inside the receive callback, before the ACK, despite a per-step quantum
